Formulation:
Predisposing: Personal and family history of anxiety  
Precipitating: 2-month period of increased work demands, late nights, possible dehydration and sleep deprivation  
Perpetuating: Ongoing workload, inadequate sleep hygiene, limited coping strategies  
Protective: Regular exercise, supportive partner, insight, willingness to engage with counselling  

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Generalised Anxiety Disorder with work-stress exacerbation
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce anxiety at work; achieve manageable workload; improve sleep
- Clinical Goal(s): Decrease baseline anxiety symptoms; enhance coping skills; maintain medication adherence
- Actions (Patient):
  • Self-refer to local counselling service (link provided)  
  • Implement sleep hygiene (7–8 h/night)  
  • Maintain hydration (1.5–2 L fluids/day)  
  • Take planned week off work (self-certify)  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide counselling service details and referral pathway  
  • Review Sertraline effectiveness and tolerance at follow-up  
  • Offer fit note if extended leave required  
  • Schedule follow-up in 1 week (phone)

Secondary Problem: Stress-related headache (probable migraine/tension-type)
- Patient Goal(s): Relieve current headache; prevent recurrence
- Clinical Goal(s): Assess headache response to first-line treatment; monitor for red-flag symptoms
- Actions (Patient):
  • Start Ibuprofen as first-line (plus optional Paracetamol) – follow dosing instructions  
  • Monitor for danger signs (link provided) and seek urgent review if present  
  • Continue regular exercise within comfort limits  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Educate on migraine vs tension-type features and trigger management  
  • Provide written information on red-flag headache symptoms  
  • Arrange blood tests/imaging if headache persists or worsens at review

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Headache danger signs, hydration, sleep hygiene, stress management, counselling options
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating anxiety, insomnia, persistent or worsening headaches, emergence of suicidal thoughts
- Coping Strategies: Scheduled breaks, exercise, relaxation techniques, timely workload planning, counselling engagement

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Obtained verbally during call
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Will be sent via electronic records portal
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: To be confirmed on counselling self-referral
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: 1 week from today (exact date to be scheduled by patient)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine without aura – High likelihood: Unilateral severe pain, photophobia, stress/sleep deprivation trigger
- Tension-type headache – Medium likelihood: Ongoing work stress, prior similar frontal headaches
- Adjustment Disorder with anxiety – Medium likelihood: Anxiety symptoms temporally related to recent work stress
